title: If you haven’t read it yet “the art of game design” is everything I was missing learning game dev with ai
author: Charming_You_25
selftext:
Has anyone else read this? I was feeling close to a wall and unsure how to make my game more cohesive. I am inspired by the book and it helped me sharpen my design.

It doesnt mention ai specifically but a huge amount of it is very relevant to ai game dev if you translate it a bit. It covers a huge amount of the skill that your agent can’t do and doesn’t prod you to do.

If anyone’s interested I’ll see if I can pull specific suggestions / what they mean in an ai development context.

comments.author: JeeCharns
comments.body: Who is it by / can you share a link? I’d be interested in your take on what it was specifically that helped you push your game further

replies.author: Tycoon33
replies.body:
The Art of Game Design  
Book by Jesse Schell

comments.author: FutureLynx_
comments.body: isnt there anything more uptodate seems thats a book from 2008

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body: Yes, a new version just came out like within a month

replies.author: PersonOfInterest007
replies.body: 3rd edition is from 2020. But it’s about game design, and the vast majority of it will be valid and useful decades from now, even if games are running on neural processors spliced into your optic nerves.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
A little hint for you. Set up an LLM wiki and then import this book and anything else you find relevant, cross reference it all and then point your favourite agent at it with a skill.

Hey presto, your agents now have some specific knowledge on how to make games. I've got several design books, some software development basics and the whole scrum.org reference in my wiki. Finding PDF versions of popular books is pretty easy.

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: This seems like wasting context, LLMs are already trained on all existing human knowledge so game design is well represented in the training data. I find Opus 5.5 has great insights on game design, level design, mechanics, balance, etc. right out of the box.

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body: Yeah, I think some things could be made into triggerable to skills or project documentation. But there is definitely a lot in the book that I as the game designer need to do or mental models that help me manage the agents that my agents can’t do. Turns out Game Design is not a solved thing yet. Agents mostly only do well with solved things.

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: Oh I’m not saying you shouldn’t read the book, you absolutely should and I may look into it too. I’m just saying current frontier models already know all of this stuff. But there is still tremendous value in learning more because you can drive AI towards a better result. Th more you know about game design, art, coding etc. the better you can direct AI even if it’s doing the actual implementation work.

replies.author: daddywookie
replies.body:
One rule of using the wiki is that the agent needs to say which sources it has used to make a decision. I can then go and validate the approach.

It was also important, while building the wiki, that I reviewed a summary of each chapter and how it added to the growing network of ideas. I learned at the same time as the wiki and could ask questions and suggest new connections. Now all that work is on hand whenever my agents need it.

It was certainly an investment but I’m glad I did it. It is used constantly throughout my production cycle from planning to design, development and testing. I need to work out how to add more visual design references now.

replies.author: daddywookie
replies.body:
There are two benefits.

The first comes from how you construct the wiki, what you link together and how you use that to create new synthesise of ideas. The wiki becomes an extension of your own philosophies and practices. I find this better than the “average of all internets” that you usually get.

The second is consistency. With the wiki as the rule book your agents can focus better on how you want to build, regardless of model or project. I found this approach totally stopped Sol from going on long winded meanders and Astra is better at keeping scope under control.

replies.author: taisui
replies.body: Claude is pretty good at rubber ducking

replies.author: YoghiThorn
replies.body: Its not a waste of context if you're using a decent memory/context management system that supports progressive disclosure.

comments.author: dgeisert
comments.body: It is a great book.  I met the author because we were both making VR sword fighting games at the same time and ended up at a few of the same conferences.  Everything in there still applies to AI game development.  The thing that probably matters most that you can't just program into the AI is getting good feedback cycles from players.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body: The trick with game design resources is to read them all. They are all different, nobody aligns, nobody is really right or wrong, and they all have a different focus. But at some point you form an intuition for things that simply can't be formalized as rigid rules.

comments.author: reality_comes
comments.body: Claude, consider the book, the art of game design when building the game

comments.author: A_Sword_Saint
comments.body: This is a classic textbook on game design that's required reading in many college game design majors.

comments.author: warorgyman
comments.body: "Read this book, generate a markdown file that you can use as context on how to develop games"

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body: It will only be able to use half the book and may have unintended consequences (starting off agile dev for example). Most of the book is for the designer- ie me

comments.author: nhami
comments.body:
Theory of Fun by Ralph Koster is great.

Both these books exploded my mind and got me in gamedev.

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body: I also have that one, I’m a few chapters in but it isn’t hitting like Art of. I think I don’t like the minimalist design of the book. I’ll definitely finish it though.
